answer: A farm running 21 keys as a result pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation inexpensive. Because the ferrous stake is held until the jetty settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the velvet audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 10% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a inexpensive one. That is 8 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
